items.author: dhxwhy
items.name: Comparing Radio Cards – Plan Picker that Shows the Difference from Your Selection
items.description: Comparing Radio Cards for React and Tailwind CSS (shadcn/ui): plan cards in a radio group where the selected card lifts forward and the others show their difference from it as chips (+$12/mo, +200 GB). It is built to answer "what changes if I pick this one" without a table. On a new pick the ring slides over, the detail unfolds and chips roll to the new baseline. Real radio inputs, controlled or uncontrolled value, numeric attributes with betterDirection, a live summary, light and dark, instant under reduced motion. Use it for pricing plans, storage tiers, shipping or seats. The included demo scripts three Alder plans and makes no requests. Requires React only, with no animation library.

items.author: dhxwhy
items.name: Early Access Pass CTA – Email Signup Section that Issues a Holographic Pass
items.description: Early Access Pass CTA for React and Tailwind CSS (shadcn/ui): an email signup section that issues a membership-style pass on submit, printing the name, rolling the number up and stamping the date. It is built to turn a signup into something visitors can hold. The pass tilts toward the pointer with a moving sheen; the form validates the address, shows Try again when the promise rejects and announces the issue politely. Controlled or uncontrolled pass, split or stacked layout, reduced motion, light and dark. Use it for waitlists, newsletters, betas and event registration. The included demo types, issues, retries once and makes no requests. Requires React only, with no animation library.

items.author: dhxwhy
items.name: Metro Map Image Gallery – Subway Map Roadmap Timeline
items.description: Metro Map Image Gallery for React and Tailwind CSS (shadcn/ui): a subway map roadmap timeline where every station is a photo and small trains run the lines. It is built to turn a list of milestones into a transit map people want to explore. Use it for product roadmaps, release timelines, travel stories and portfolios, with milestones as stations on up to five colored lines. Trains brake into each stop and pop its photo in a bubble; hovering a station grows the photo into a card and fades the other lines, and a click opens a dialog with a large photo, the story and the next stop. Pass active, open, onActiveChange, onOpenChange, trainSpeed, dwell, autoplay and labels for controlled or uncontrolled use. Stations are buttons with one tab stop and arrow keys along and across lines, the dialog traps focus and closes on Escape, reduced motion parks the trains, and light and dark themes plus a portrait phone layout are built in. The included demo rides a fictional 2026 product roadmap and makes no requests beyond image loads. Requires React only, with no animation library.

items.author: dhxwhy
items.name: Color Palette Image Gallery – Extract and Filter by Palette
items.description: Color Palette Image Gallery for React and Tailwind CSS (shadcn/ui): pull a five-color palette out of every photo, then filter photos by color. It is built to let visitors shop by color: pick a real shade in one photo and see which others share it. Use it for mood boards, shop-by-color filters, fashion and interior stores, and portfolios. Hover a photo and its palette fans out like paint chips with HEX labels; press a swatch and matching photos lift with a color dot as the rest sink to grayscale, and a header pill lets you copy the HEX. Palettes come from your data or the built-in color palette extractor (canvas, k-means in OKLab); photos without CORS skip it. The palette picker is controlled or uncontrolled (value, onChange), with onSelect, threshold, columns and labels. Photos are roving-tabindex buttons (arrows move, Enter pins, Escape folds); reduced motion drops transitions, and both themes use shadcn tokens. The included demo autoplays a palette tour over 16 stock photos and makes no requests beyond image loads. Requires React and lucide-react, with no animation library.

items.author: dhxwhy
items.name: Pendant Lamp Rail Gallery – Lighting Store Hero Section
items.description: Pendant Lamp Rail Gallery for React and Tailwind CSS (shadcn/ui): pendant lamps on a brushed aluminum ceiling track that switch on as you brush past them. It is built to make a lighting store feel like a real showroom, so visitors switch a lamp on, see its glow on the wall and stay to compare. Use it for lighting stores, home decor and interior e-commerce, product showcases and hero sections. Each lamp crossfades to its switched-on photo with a warm pool, beam and bloom on the wall; the cords swing with pendulum physics, longer cords slower. Drag a pendant along the track to push its neighbors; click or press Enter to lift it into a detail view whose dimmer sets the glow. Items take name, description, image, imageOn, drop, glow, tag and details; control the lit lamp with active and onActiveChange, listen with onOpenChange and translate labels. Keyboard roving focus, an accessible modal, touch swipe, reduced motion and light and dark themes are built in. The included demo hangs eight pendants and makes no requests beyond image loads. Requires React only, with no animation library.

items.author: dhxwhy
items.name: Picture Rail Image Gallery – Art Print Shop Hero Section
items.description: Picture Rail Image Gallery for React and Tailwind CSS (shadcn/ui): framed prints hanging from a picture rail on steel wires. It is built to make an art print shop or portfolio feel like a real gallery wall, so visitors stop, touch a print and look closer. Use it for art print stores, photo shops, artist portfolios and hero sections. Each frame hangs from its hook as a pendulum with real physics (longer wires swing slower); a hover tilt leans the print toward the pointer, its picture light switches on and the wall dims. Drag a print along the rail to bump its neighbours; click or press Enter to lift it off the wall and turn it to read the gallery label on the back. Items take title, artist, year, image, aspect, frame, mat, drop, tag and details; control the lit print with active and onActiveChange, track the dialog with onOpenChange, relabel it with labels. Roving keyboard focus, an accessible modal, reduced motion and light/dark themes are built in. The included demo hangs eight framed prints and makes no requests beyond image loads. Requires React only, with no animation library.

items.author: dhxwhy
items.name: Product Rail Gallery – Fashion Store Hero Section
items.description: Product Rail Gallery, a fashion store hero section for React and Tailwind CSS (shadcn/ui): real garment photos hang from wooden hangers on a clothing rail (a clothing rack, in American English), turn to face the shopper on hover, slide along the rail with hanger physics, and lift off the rail to show the back. It is made for e-commerce: online clothing stores, fashion and apparel brands, streetwear drops and lookbooks that want a shop hero and product showcase shoppers can handle like a rack in a store. Each piece takes a front, back and side photo (transparent PNG or WebP) or falls back to built-in illustrations for tees, knits, hoodies, shirts, jackets and coats. The rail is a one-dimensional physics simulation: dragging a hanger pushes its neighbours, released pieces swing and settle, and the hovered piece turns with a perspective rotation. Keyboard users get a roving tabindex with arrow keys, Home/End and Enter; touch users tap to turn and tap again to lift; the detail view is an accessible modal with Escape, focus trapping and focus return. Autoplay, interval, hanger style, labels and an onOpenChange callback are props. Light and dark mode, prefers-reduced-motion, no dependencies beyond React.

items.author: dhxwhy
items.name: Sushi Conveyor Belt Menu – Restaurant Hero Section
items.description: Sushi Conveyor Belt Menu – Restaurant Hero Section for React and Tailwind CSS (shadcn/ui): a kaiten sushi belt that keeps turning plates round a stadium-shaped loop. It is built to make a restaurant menu something visitors play with: hover to stop the belt, flick to spin it, pick a plate to order. Use it for restaurant and food ordering pages. A physics belt eases to a stop under the pointer and lifts the plate with a name and price chip; a drag scrubs it and a flick spins on with inertia before settling to cruise speed. A picked plate flies into a dialog with details and an Add to order button. Price tiers become colour-coded plate rings with a legend; active, paused, onActiveChange, onOpenChange, onAdd, speed and labels control it. One roving tab stop with arrow keys, a focus-trapped dialog closed by Escape, a pause button, reduced motion that steps plate by plate, light and dark themes. The included demo runs an eight-plate lunch belt with an order counter and makes no requests beyond image loads. Requires React only, with no animation library; the demo adds a lucide-react icon.

items.author: dhxwhy
items.name: Team Lanyard Rail – Meet the Team Section with Flip Badges
items.description: Team Lanyard Rail for React and Tailwind CSS (shadcn/ui): a meet the team section where lanyard ID badges hang from a brushed rail and flip over to introduce each person. It is built to make an about page feel tactile, so visitors meet the team by pulling and flipping badges instead of scanning a grid of avatars. Use it for about pages, team sections, hero sections, portfolios and hiring pages. Badges sway with spring physics: hover turns one to the front and nudges its neighbours, dragging slides it along the rail with collisions, pulling it down stretches the reel cord before it bounces back, and a click turns it over, flip card style, to a bio, tags and contact links. Items take name, role, team, photo, bio, tags, links and a chart-color tone; active and flipped can be controlled with callbacks. Keyboard support, an aria-live caption, reduced motion, light and dark themes and a swipe carousel on phones are built in. The included demo autoplays a short tour of eight fictional teammates and makes no requests beyond image loads. Requires React only, with no animation library.

items.author: dhxwhy
items.name: Wordmark Reveal Footer – Giant Logo Footer with Reflection, Status and Local Time
items.description: Wordmark Reveal Footer for React and Tailwind CSS (shadcn/ui): a footer whose giant wordmark rises letter by letter through the floor line, lights a reflection, then switches on a status band with live local time per office. It is built to close a page with a brand moment that feels alive instead of a static logo. Props: brand, columns, newsletter, socials, legal, status tone, offices with IANA time zones, reflection, reveal on mount, in view or manual, controlled revealed with onRevealEnd. Landmarks, reduced motion, light and dark. Use it for SaaS, studio and agency sites. The included demo replays the reveal once and makes no requests. Requires React only, with no animation library.

items.author: kedhareswer
items.name: Interactive Boarding Pass Ticket Card
items.description: Interactive boarding pass ticket card with a front and back: a VIP pass with a halftone Moon and a paper boarding pass with a perforated stub you can tear off. Tilt, flip and personalise every field through props. Use it for event tickets, launch invites or a playful hero.

items.author: kedhareswer
items.name: Handwriting Signature Footer
items.description: Handwriting signature footer: a white stylus writes one word in flowing script stroke by stroke, lifts and rests beside it, then a thank-you line, a short note, two actions and a quiet legal bar settle in. Built-in single-stroke script glyphs, no fonts or images. For signing flows, checkouts and case studies.
